evals.name: omitzero-vs-omitempty
evals.prompt:
Review these JSON struct tags for correctness in our Go 1.24 API. Users report that zero-value time fields and false booleans are unexpectedly included or omitted in JSON responses.

```go
package api

import "time"

type Event struct {
    ID        string    `json:"id"`
    Name      string    `json:"name"`
    StartAt   time.Time `json:"start_at,omitempty"`
    EndAt     time.Time `json:"end_at,omitempty"`
    Cancelled bool      `json:"cancelled,omitempty"`
    Archived  bool      `json:"archived,omitempty"`
    Notes     string    `json:"notes,omitempty"`
    Priority  int       `json:"priority,omitempty"`
}

type UserSettings struct {
    UserID           string    `json:"user_id"`
    DarkMode         bool      `json:"dark_mode,omitempty"`
    EmailNotifs      bool      `json:"email_notifs,omitempty"`
    LastLogin        time.Time `json:"last_login,omitempty"`
    AccountCreated   time.Time `json:"account_created,omitempty"`
    Bio              string    `json:"bio,omitempty"`
}
```

Explain the issue and provide the corrected code.
evals.trap: omitempty doesn't work correctly for time.Time (zero time is a non-empty struct) and treats false as empty for bool. Go 1.24 introduced omitzero which handles both correctly. Without the skill, the model may not know about omitzero.

assertions.text: Identifies that omitempty doesn't omit zero time.Time (it's a non-empty struct)
Suggests omitzero for time.Time fields (StartAt, EndAt, LastLogin, AccountCreated)
Identifies that omitempty treats false as empty for bool fields
Addresses bool issue correctly (removes tag or uses omitzero)
Correctly notes omitzero requires Go 1.24+
Does NOT suggest omitzero for string or int fields where omitempty works correctly

evals.name: addcleanup-vs-setfinalizer
evals.trap: New Go code should consider runtime.AddCleanup instead of runtime.SetFinalizer because it is less error-prone. The key API difference: AddCleanup takes the resource as a separate argument (not the whole object). Without the skill the model is unlikely to know AddCleanup exists or that SetFinalizer's cycle restriction is a major problem.

assertions.text: Replaces runtime.SetFinalizer with runtime.AddCleanup
AddCleanup cleanup function receives the resource (db/*sql.DB or fd/int) as a separate argument, NOT the whole wrapper struct
Explains that SetFinalizer prevents GC when the object holds a reference to itself or another object with a finalizer (cycle restriction)
Does NOT pass ManagedConn or TempFile directly as the resource to AddCleanup
Correctly attributes runtime.AddCleanup to Go 1.24 (or notes it is the modern replacement)

evals.name: http-mux-migration

assertions.text: Uses http.NewServeMux() instead of mux.NewRouter()
Uses method prefix in patterns like 'GET /api/users/{id}'
Uses r.PathValue("id") instead of mux.Vars(r)
All 6 routes migrated with correct method prefixes (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE)
No gorilla/mux import remains
Return type changes from *mux.Router to *http.ServeMux

Uses synctest.Wait() for goroutine synchronization

evals.name: json-v2-duplicate-key-strictness
evals.trap: encoding/json now runs on top of encoding/json/v2 by default since Go 1.27, and v2 rejects duplicate object member names instead of silently keeping the last one like v1 did. Without the skill, the model may not connect the Go 1.27 bump to this specific new decode-time failure and may guess at unrelated causes (malformed JSON, network issues).

assertions.text: Identifies that Go 1.27 made encoding/json/v2 the default JSON implementation underneath encoding/json
Explains that duplicate JSON object keys are now rejected by default, whereas v1 silently kept the last value
Connects the partner payload's duplicate id key directly to the reported decode failures
Proposes a concrete fix: either normalize/dedupe the payload before decoding, or explicitly opts back into v1 behavior only as a temporary bridge
Names GOEXPERIMENT=nojsonv2 as an escape hatch, not as the recommended long-term fix
Does NOT claim encoding/json's decode behavior is unaffected by upgrading to Go 1.27

evals.name: generic-method-scoped-transform
evals.trap: Go 1.27 lets methods declare their own type parameters, so a transform from Set[T] to Set[U] can be a method on Set[T] with U scoped to the method. Without the skill, the natural default is a package-level generic function `func MapSet[T, U comparable](s Set[T], f func(T) U) Set[U]` because pre-1.27 Go had no way to add a type parameter to a method.

assertions.text: Declares the transform as a method on Set[T] (e.g. func (s Set[T]) Map[U comparable](f func(T) U) Set[U]) rather than a standalone package-level generic function
The new type parameter (U) is declared on the method itself, not added to the Set[T] type definition
Notes that generic methods declaring their own type parameters are a Go 1.27 addition
Calls out that this method could not satisfy an interface method and that interface methods themselves cannot declare type parameters
The example call site compiles conceptually (correct method call syntax with explicit or inferred U)

evals.name: godebug-removed-key-build-break
evals.prompt:
Upgrade this project to the latest stable Go toolchain and update `go.mod` accordingly.

```
module example.com/svc

go 1.24

godebug (
    asynctimerchan=0
)

require (
    github.com/lib/pq v1.10.9
)
```

The `asynctimerchan=0` line was added a while ago to keep `time.Timer`/`time.Ticker` channels buffered like they were before Go 1.23, because some code relied on a stale timer value still sitting in the channel. Provide the updated `go.mod`.
evals.trap: Go 1.27 removed the asynctimerchan GODEBUG setting entirely; a go.mod godebug entry still pinning it to its old (pre-1.23) value now fails the build, not just prints a warning. The natural default without the skill is to bump only the go directive and leave the godebug block untouched, assuming an old GODEBUG pin is harmless leftover config.

assertions.text: Removes or updates the asynctimerchan=0 godebug entry rather than leaving it as-is
Explains that Go 1.27 removed this GODEBUG setting and that a go.mod entry pinned to the old value now fails the build (not just a warning)
Bumps the go directive to a current Go 1.27-era version
Recommends actually fixing the underlying code that relied on buffered timer channels rather than just deleting the compatibility shim silently
Mentions checking for other Go 1.27-removed GODEBUG keys (e.g. tls3des, gotypesalias, tlsrsakex) as part of the same upgrade, not just asynctimerchan

evals.name: go127-synctest-http
evals.trap: testing/synctest makes time-based tests deterministic, but a plain httptest.NewServer uses the real network, which stalls inside a synctest bubble (the bubble's fake clock waits forever on real I/O). Go 1.27 added httptest.NewTestServer, which runs on an in-memory fake network designed for synctest. Without the skill, the model either avoids synctest (retries/channels) or combines synctest with httptest.NewServer, producing a hanging test.

assertions.text: Wraps tests in synctest.Test
Uses httptest.NewTestServer instead of httptest.NewServer
Explains that real-network servers do not work inside a synctest bubble (in-memory/fake network rationale)
Does NOT leave a plain httptest.NewServer inside a synctest bubble
Keeps both tests working (response test and client-timeout test) with deterministic time
